body:
**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

I think because "a" is part of MyEntity, you'd want to Load(MyEntity).load_only('a').    It probably should work the way you're doing it also, but using ``Load`` explicitly is not that common of a use case so I'd stick with unbound.

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* added labels: **low priority**

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* changed **title** from "Load.load_only on polymorphic child doesn't work" to "Load.load_only based on subclass doesn't get recog"

**Dmytro Starosud ([@dima-starosud](https://github.com/dima-starosud)) wrote:**

> I think because "a" is part of MyEntity, you'd want to Load(MyEntity).load_only('a').

Looks like it's not really true:
```
class MyChild(MyEntity):
    __mapper_args__ = {'polymorphic_identity': 'child_1'}
    c = column_property(func.true())

print(Query(MyChild).options(Load(MyChild).load_only('c')))
```
produces full query
```
SELECT true() AS true_1, my_entity.id AS my_entity_id, my_entity.a AS my_entity_a, my_entity.b AS my_entity_b, my_entity.kind AS my_entity_kind
FROM my_entity
WHERE my_entity.kind IN (:kind_1)
```

BTW, It works with `aliased`:

```
my_child = aliased(MyChild)
print(Query(my_child).options(Load(my_child).load_only('a')))
```
produces
```
SELECT my_entity_1.id AS my_entity_1_id, my_entity_1.a AS my_entity_1_a, my_entity_1.kind AS my_entity_1_kind
FROM my_entity AS my_entity_1
WHERE my_entity_1.kind IN (:kind_1)
```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

i meant, ``Load(MyEntity).load_only("a")``.   a column_property() on a single-inh subclass is not a use case we have a lot of tests for and that sounds like a separate issue.

OK this works for the "unbound" version because of #3287 committed in b63aae2c232f980a47aa2a635c35dfa45390f451 where an explicit "add the option for superclasses" step was added, when you have `query(MyChild).options(load_only('*'))`.  This logic is not used for `query(MyChild).options(Load(MyChild).load_only('*'))`, which is likely because I didn't attend as much to the `Load()` cases, which may have been either because I overlooked it or that maybe I felt that `Load(MyChild)` is more specific, but it's not clear if that's true or not.  For example, what would we expect if `MyChlid` has column attributes of its own?  Would we expect `Load(MyChild).load_only('a')` to exclude only columns local to `MyChild` ?  probably not.   But this is a behavior change so if I can get it working it will be only for 1.3.

OK that was easy

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
index af9bd71b6a..0ef34b0b9b 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
@@ -357,9 +357,15 @@ class Load(Generative, MapperOption):
         else:
             effective_path = self.path
 
-        self._set_for_path(
-            self.context, effective_path, replace=True,
-            merge_opts=self.is_opts_only)
+        if effective_path.is_token:
+            for path in effective_path.generate_for_superclasses():
+                self._set_for_path(
+                    self.context, path, replace=True,
+                    merge_opts=self.is_opts_only)
+        else:
+            self._set_for_path(
+                self.context, effective_path, replace=True,
+                merge_opts=self.is_opts_only)
 
     def __getstate__(self):
         d = self.__dict__.copy()

```

issue.title: wildcard loader options are not documented for columns, other features missing

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

issue.body: in https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_09.html#class-specific-wildcards we talk about the new wildcard feature, but that's not the main docs.  There's a little bit of wildcard mentioned at https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/orm/loading_relationships.html?highlight=wildcard#wildcard-loading-strategies.  But nothing for columns at https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/orm/loading_columns.html - there's "load_only()" which is what uses wildcards behind the scenes, but it should be mentioned.  but then what gets really weird is, what's this?  https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/master/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py#L495  "dot-star" ?  what's that ?   I don't even know what it does and I implemented it. no docs anywhere for that?  that's kind of a problem b.c i dont even know what it does.

body:
**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue:

**Apply path generation for superclasses to Load._set_path_strategy()** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/991

issue.title: Using load_only on joinedload for polymorphic relation loads more columns

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

labels.name: inheritance
labels.description: issues to do wtih ORM inheritance, a particularly tricky area

issue.body:
This is using sqlalchemy==1.2.16

Following snippet produces SQL that loads more attributes (other_attribute) than was asked for:

```
from sqlalchemy import Column, ForeignKey, Integer, Unicode, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import Query, relationship, joinedload
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

engine = create_engine(
    'mysql://**',
    poolclass=NullPool
)

connection = engine.connect()
connection.begin()

Base = declarative_base()


class Context(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'context'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    context_type = Column(Unicode(256), nullable=False)

    parent = relationship('Context')

    parent_id = Column(
        Integer, ForeignKey(
            'context.id'
        ), nullable=True
    )
    __mapper_args__ = {'polymorphic_on': context_type}


class Task(Context):
    __tablename__ = 'task'
    __mapper_args__ = {'polymorphic_identity': 'child1'}
    id = Column(
        Integer,
        ForeignKey('context.id'),
        primary_key=True
    )


class Project(Context):
    __tablename__ = 'project'

    id = Column(
        Integer,
        ForeignKey('context.id'),
        primary_key=True
    )

    full_name = Column(Unicode(256))

    other_attribute = Column(Unicode(256))


Base.metadata.create_all(connection)

query = Query(Task).options(
    joinedload(Task.parent.of_type(Project)).load_only('full_name')
)

print(query)
```

The following query is produced:

`
SELECT task.id AS task_id, context.id AS context_id, context.context_type AS context_context_type, context.parent_id AS context_parent_id, anon_1.context_id AS anon_1_context_id, anon_1.context_context_type AS anon_1_context_context_type, anon_1.project_id AS anon_1_project_id, anon_1.project_full_name AS anon_1_project_full_name, anon_1.project_other_attribute AS anon_1_project_other_attribute
FROM context JOIN task ON context.id = task.id LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT context.id AS context_id, context.context_type AS context_context_type, context.parent_id AS context_parent_id, project.id AS project_id, project.full_name AS project_full_name, project.other_attribute AS project_other_attribute
FROM context LEFT OUTER JOIN project ON context.id = project.id) AS anon_1 ON context.id = anon_1.context_parent_id
`

Where as sqlalchemy==1.1.4 gave, which omits other_attribute in the outer select:

`
SELECT task.id AS task_id, context.id AS context_id, context.context_type AS context_context_type, context.parent_id AS context_parent_id, anon_1.context_id AS anon_1_context_id, anon_1.context_context_type AS anon_1_context_context_type, anon_1.project_id AS anon_1_project_id, anon_1.project_full_name AS anon_1_project_full_name
FROM context JOIN task ON context.id = task.id LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT context.id AS context_id, context.context_type AS context_context_type, context.parent_id AS context_parent_id, project.id AS project_id, project.full_name AS project_full_name, project.other_attribute AS project_other_attribute
FROM context LEFT OUTER JOIN project ON context.id = project.id) AS anon_1 ON context.id = anon_1.context_parent_id
`

I've been trying with more explicit alias and with_polymorphic approaches, but it gives same result.
